planting.note: Set out container-grown plants after the last frost into well-drained beds, giving them room to spread into a wide mounding mass by midsummer.

directions: Plant in ordinary, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost, allowing room for its wide mounding spread. Irene was bred at the University of Florida as a sterile, low-seed-set lantana developed to reduce the escape of wild-type Lantana camara into natural areas along the Gulf Coast. Its rounded flower clusters open in hot pink and gold that blend together across each truss, drawing steady butterfly traffic through the heat of summer into fall. Treat it as a root-hardy perennial in the mildest zones, cutting frost-damaged stems back hard in late winter to renew dense new growth.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs after the last frost in acidic, moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Maui Red blooms most heavily in full sun and needs consistently warm temperatures.

directions: Plant in acidic, moist, well-drained soil in full sun. Maui Red is the red-flowered counterpart to the yellow-orange Maui ixora, sharing the same compact, small-leaved, densely branching habit topped with rounded clusters of small, star-shaped, brick-red flowers produced over a long warm-season bloom period. Its tidy, slow-growing form suits foundation plantings, low hedges, and containers where a full-size ixora would quickly outgrow the space. Keep soil consistently moist but well drained, feed with an acid-forming fertilizer to prevent the yellowing ixora shows in alkaline soil, and protect plants from any frost.

common_name: French Vanilla Marigold (AAS-Winning Tall Creamy-White American Marigold)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost in full sun in well-drained soil; French Vanilla is a tall American marigold selection whose sturdy, well-branched plants need more room than compact bedding types.

directions: French Vanilla is a 1985 All-America Selections winner notable for introducing a soft creamy-white color into the tall American marigold class, a shade rarely seen at the time against the gold, orange, and yellow flowers typical of the species. Plants grow tall and well-branched with sturdy stems, carrying large, fully double blooms held well above the foliage on strong stalks that hold up in wind and rain better than many older tall types. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, space generously to let the vigorous plants fill out, and deadhead spent flowers regularly to keep new buds forming through the season. Its height and pale color make it useful as a back-of-border accent or cut flower, pairing well with darker orange or maroon-toned marigolds for contrast.

common_name: Victoria White Salvia (White-Flowered Companion to Victoria Blue Mealy Sage)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6–8 weeks before transplanting or plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to average, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Victoria White is grown identically to Victoria Blue and the two are frequently interplanted for a two-tone bedding display.

directions: Victoria White is the white-flowered counterpart to the classic Victoria Blue selection of Salvia farinacea, sharing the same dense, upright flower spikes and soft white-mealy coating on the stems and calyces that gives mealy sage its common name, but replacing Victoria Blue's deep violet-blue color with clean white blooms. Growers commonly interplant the two side by side for a crisp blue-and-white bedding scheme, since both share identical height, habit, and bloom timing. In Gulf South gardens it behaves as a short-lived perennial that may persist a few years with mild winters or as a long-lived annual from spring transplants, blooming from late spring through frost with excellent heat tolerance. Deadhead or shear lightly after the first flush to encourage rebloom, and use the cut spikes in fresh arrangements, where they hold their color well after cutting.
